question: According to publicly available information, the City of Oldenburg (Germany) intends to finance the construction of a new stadium at an estimated cost of approximately EUR 77 million and with annual operating deficits exceeding EUR 3 million. The municipal administration stated that a State aid notification was submitted to the Commission on 4 February 2026.
Given the significant public funding involved and the potential conferral of a selective economic advantage on professional users of the infrastructure, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
Can it confirm whether a notification or pre-notification procedure concerning this project is currently ongoing?

Under which legal basis is the measure being assessed, in particular Article 55 of the General Block Exemption Regulation or Article 107(3) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and on what legal and economic grounds does the Commission consider that public financing of sports infrastructure primarily benefiting a professional football club may be compatible with the internal market despite the selective advantage it confers and its potential to distort competition?

Has the Commission identified any preliminary concerns regarding the compatibility of the financing model with State aid rules, notably in relation to the full municipal financing of the infrastructure and the projected recurring operating deficits, and can the Commission provide an indicative timeline for the assessment?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.7.2026) The Commission is currently assessing a State aid measure to finance the construction of a new stadium in the German city of Oldenburg. The investigation is ongoing and the Commission has not yet reached a conclusion as to the compatibility of the measure with the internal market.

The Commission is in close contact with the relevant Member State to gather all necessary information. In accordance with its standard practice, the Commission does not comment on ongoing investigations to preserve the confidentiality of the procedure and the rights of the Member State concerned. The Commission will adopt a decision once its assessment has been completed.
